newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU members to opt for "status quo" over car parts.
newsitem.headline: EU members to opt for "status quo" over car parts.

text.p: European Union member states are expected to opt on Tuesday to continue the current system used to protect industrial designs and models rather than introduce harmonisation at EU level.
A qualified majority at the Internal Market Council is expected to take this line, which will ensure a hotch-potch of national rules for spare parts for cars continues.
The result is expected to annoy the European Commission which had set its sights on harmonisation in this area and had modified its position to accommodate amendments by the European Parliament.
Under the current system, larger car manufacturers are able to protect spare parts from copying by independent manufacturers.

The Commission had proposed modifying the so-called "repairs clause" of the draft directive to mean that smaller manufacturers could copy so-called "visible" parts like doors and headlights under a licence system, as long as they paid the original manufacturer an equitable and reasonable fee.
The Commission says that the plans are needed to encourage investment.
So-called "non-visible" parts would not be protected.
Only Austria was willing to accept the system proposed by the Commission. The others are expected on Tuesday to accept the Irish compromise to leave the system as it is.
